# ListView

Header: `winui/ui/collections/ListView.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/collections/ListView.hpp`.

A vertical, virtualized, selectable list of templated items.

Each item sits in a container with rounded chrome: a backplate for hover and press, a 3 pixel accent selection indicator in Single and Extended mode, and a check box per item in Multiple mode. Items, templates, selection, groups, header and footer, drag reordering and scrolling come from [ListViewBase](list-view-base.md#uilistviewbase).

Example: 
```cpp
// Declarative: the items and how one row looks (plain strings need no `.item`).
std::vector<std::string> fruits{"Apple", "Banana", "Cherry"};
ui::Control<ui::ListView<std::string>> list;
window.set_content(ui::ListView<std::string>{
    .items                = fruits,
    .selection_mode       = ui::SelectionMode::Single,
    .height               = 240.0f,
    .on_selection_changed = [&](std::optional<std::string> fruit)
    { std::println("selected {}", fruit ? *fruit : "nothing"); },
    .control              = list,
    .item                 = [](const std::string& fruit) -> ui::Spec {
        return ui::Text{.text = fruit};
    },
});

// Imperative:
auto stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto names = std::make_unique<ui::ListViewControl>();
names->set_items({"One", "Two", "Three"});
names->set_item_click_enabled(true);
names->on_item_click([](std::size_t i) { std::println("clicked {}", i); });
stack->add(std::move(names));
```

## `ui::ListView`

A virtualized, selectable list of rows. Builds a [ui::ListViewControl](#uilistviewcontrol).

[`.items`](#uilistview-items) is the collection and [`.item`](#uilistview-item) is how one row looks. The handlers receive the item they are about. Only rows in view are realized, so [`.item`](#uilistview-item) runs per visible row. An item type that is text (`std::string`) needs no [`.item`](#uilistview-item).

[`.items`](#uilistview-items) takes the same three sources as [ui::ForEach](for-each.md#uiforeach), and the list follows the first two:

- A [ui::ObservableVector<T>](../core/observable-vector.md): every insert, removal and move reaches the list as that change, and [`.item`](#uilistview-item) may take the item as `T&`.
- A [`ui::Property<std::vector<T>>`](../core/property.md): with [`.key`](#uilistview-key), a reorder is followed as moves, so the selection stays on its item through a sort or a filter. A change that needs very many moves, such as a shuffle of several thousand items, arrives as one reset instead, which rebuilds the rows and clears the selection. Without [`.key`](#uilistview-key), the rows before and after an edit are kept.
- A plain `std::vector<T>` or a braced list, copied once.

A reorder by the user ([`can_reorder_items`](#uilistview-can_reorder_items)) is written back. An [ObservableVector](../core/observable-vector.md) is moved in place, and a bound [Property](../core/property.md) is assigned the reordered vector.

Name the item type, as in [`ui::ListView<Contact>`](#uilistview). C++ deduces a spec's type only from the field's own type, which a [Property](../core/property.md) or an [ObservableVector](../core/observable-vector.md) is not. The control works with indices, so through [`.control`](#uilistview-control) an item is its position in the collection.

Example: 
```cpp
struct Contact
{
    int         id = 0;
    std::string name;
    std::string company;
    friend bool operator==(const Contact&, const Contact&) = default;
};
ui::Property<std::vector<Contact>> contacts{{{1, "Ada Lovelace", "Analytical"}, {2, "Grace Hopper", "Navy"}}};
ui::Property<std::string>          status{};

window.set_content(ui::ListView<Contact>{
    .items                = contacts,
    .key                  = &Contact::id,
    .height               = 400.0f,
    .on_selection_changed = [&](std::optional<Contact> contact)
    { status = contact ? "Selected " + contact->name : ""; },
    .item                 = [](const Contact& contact) -> ui::Spec
    {
        return ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
            ui::Text{.text = contact.name},
            ui::Text{.text = contact.company, .role = ui::TextRole::Caption},
        }};
    },
});

// Plain text needs no template.
ui::ListView<std::string>{.items = {"Inbox", "Drafts", "Sent"}};
```

Any other item is valid during the call only, so capture it by value. |

### build

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<Element> build()&&
```

Consumes the spec and returns the built [ui::ListViewControl](#uilistviewcontrol); the caller owns it.

Derives from `ui::ListViewBase`.
